input_facts.text:
The BLS release labelled March 8, 2024 reports February nonfarm payroll employment up 275,000 and unemployment at 3.9%, up 0.2 percentage point.
Payroll employment comes from the establishment survey; unemployment comes from the household survey. Household employment was 161.152 million in January and 160.968 million in February; the civilian labor force was 167.276 million and 167.426 million respectively.
December payroll growth was revised from 333,000 to 290,000 and January from 353,000 to 229,000; the combined revision was -167,000. Revisions incorporate additional reports and recalculated seasonal factors.
The release describes different survey coverage and sampling precision. It gives roughly 130,000 and 600,000 as monthly-change significance thresholds for establishment and household employment, respectively.

adjudication_excerpt.text: The two surveys measure different populations and concepts, so payroll growth and a higher unemployment rate are not a same-contract contradiction. Household employment fell 184,000 while the labor force rose 150,000; their difference implies 334,000 more unemployed, subject to the release's rounding. The household employment change is below its stated approximate significance threshold; the payroll change exceeds its separate stated threshold. Those thresholds do not alone establish a recession, causality, a directional trade or confidence in every subgroup. The unemployment-rate increase is 20 basis points, not 0.2 basis points. The -167,000 revision describes prior months and must not be presented as February payroll growth; 275,000 minus 167,000 equals 108,000 arithmetically but is not the released February change. No subsequent prices, outcomes, market expectations or policy path are supplied.

question_en: Using only the supplied release, reconcile February payroll growth with the higher unemployment rate, quantify the household employment and labor-force changes and the unemployment-rate unit, explain the prior-month revisions and the separate survey sampling thresholds, and state what cannot be concluded.

expected_properties.check: Payroll employment comes from the establishment survey and unemployment from the household survey; the two measure different populations and concepts, so payroll growth together with a higher unemployment rate is not a same-contract contradiction.

Household employment fell 184,000 (161.152 million to 160.968 million) while the civilian labor force rose 150,000 (167.276 million to 167.426 million); their difference implies 334,000 more unemployed, subject to the release's rounding.

The -167,000 combined revision describes December and January; it must not be presented as February payroll growth, and 108,000 (275,000 minus 167,000) is arithmetic only, not the released February change.
Unemployment at 3.9% is up 0.2 percentage point, which is 20 basis points, not 0.2 basis points.

The roughly 130,000 and 600,000 monthly-change significance thresholds belong to the establishment and household surveys separately; the household employment change is below its stated approximate threshold while the payroll change exceeds its separate stated threshold.
Those thresholds alone establish no recession, causality, directional trade or confidence in every subgroup, and no subsequent prices, outcomes, market expectations or policy path are supplied.

known_failure_modes: Treat payroll growth and a higher unemployment rate as a same-contract contradiction, ignoring that the two surveys cover different populations and concepts.
Misstate the household arithmetic: employment fell 184,000, the labor force rose 150,000, and the implied increase in unemployed is 334,000 before rounding.
Present the -167,000 combined revision as February payroll growth, or report 108,000 as the released February change.
Call the 0.2 percentage-point unemployment-rate rise 0.2 basis points.
Apply one survey's significance threshold to the other, or read a threshold crossing as proof of recession, causality, a directional trade or subgroup confidence.
Import subsequent prices, outcomes, market expectations or a policy path that the release does not supply.
gold_standard_sentence: The establishment survey reports February payroll up 275,000 while the household survey shows unemployment at 3.9%, up 0.2 percentage point (20 basis points); these are different survey populations and concepts. Household employment fell 184,000, below its approximate 600,000 monthly-change significance threshold; the labor force rose 150,000, implying about 334,000 more unemployed subject to rounding. Payroll growth exceeds its separate approximate 130,000 threshold. The -167,000 revision belongs to December and January, not February. These facts alone establish no recession, causality, trade or policy path.
